battle.name: 制憲派戰爭
battle.brief: 維基戰爭列表所載的1931年制憲派戰爭，發生於巴西南里奧格蘭德州，為地方制憲派武裝與聯邦政府軍之間的邊境衝突。英國海軍自1877年列裝的魚雷艇（Torpedo boat）是當時已服役的水面小艇裝備，用於近岸巡邏、警戒與魚雷突擊，可擔任沿海與河口警戒任務。

kit.name: 魚雷艇
kit.history: 魚雷艇為皇家海軍早期水面小艇分類，以快速接近敵艦並施放魚雷為主要任務，平時用於近岸巡邏、警戒與護航。

countries: 制憲派戰爭發生在西班牙本土，主要戰場是首都馬德里與阿拉岡軍區首府薩拉戈薩。發動方是以將軍何塞・聖胡爾霍為核心的部分軍官及其駐軍系統，另有少數外省守軍短暫響應；守方則是掌握中央政權的西班牙第二共和國政府、首都衛戍司令部與服從中央的部隊。馬德里集中廣播、政府機關和軍政指揮中心，薩拉戈薩控制軍區行政與交通節點，兩地由鐵路、軍用電話及電報連接。其餘軍區只有零星響應，沒有形成可持續占領區，因此這不是兩軍拉鋒的常規戰爭，而是一場在多個駐軍城市同時發作、隨即被中央兵力分割各處的國內政變戰。
countriesEn: The Constitutionalist War took place entirely within Spain, with the principal fighting centered on Madrid, the national capital, and Zaragoza, the headquarters of the Aragon military region. The initiating side consisted of a group of officers centered on General Jose Sanjurjo together with elements of their garrison network; a few units in other provinces responded briefly. The defending side was the government of the Second Spanish Republic, the Madrid garrison command, and military units that obeyed the central government. Madrid contained the radio service, major government offices, and the senior military command, while Zaragoza controlled the regional administration and transport network. The two cities were connected by railway, military telephone, and telegraph lines. Since the disturbances in other military regions never developed into durable occupied zones, this was not a conventional war between established fronts. It was a domestic coup that began in several garrison cities, was severed by centrally controlled forces, and collapsed once each local rebel group was isolated.
people: 政治指揮以首相尼塞托・阿爾卡拉－薩莫拉和內政部長曼努埃爾・阿薩尼亞為核心，軍方守方則由米格爾・卡瓦涅利亞斯將軍在首都組織效忠中央的部隊。發動方由身任阿拉岡軍區首長的何塞・聖胡爾霍將軍居中串聯；聖地亞哥・索里亞諾上校率領馬德里行動小組，安東尼奧・卡斯蒂略上校在薩拉戈薩發動駐軍。數個首長雖同意奪權，基層連隊卻沒有全部跟進，使策劃者無法把政治聲望轉成統一兵力。通訊被切斷後，參與軍官只能依據本營 命令與現場指揮作決定。卡瓦涅利亞斯包圍首都叛軍據點，聖胡爾霍隨後被拘並逃往葡萄牙，於1932年缺席受審。
peopleEn: Political direction rested with Prime Minister Niceto Alcala-Zamora and Interior Minister Manuel Azana, while the loyal military response in Madrid was organized under General Miguel Cabanellas. The initiating side was coordinated by General Jose Sanjurjo in his capacity as head of the Aragon military region. Colonel Santiago Soriano led the action group in Madrid, and Colonel Antonio Castillo raised the Zaragoza garrison. Although several senior officers supported taking power, the subordinate companies did not follow as a whole, preventing the plotters from converting political influence into a coherent armed force. Once communications were cut, participating officers could only decide according to orders already held locally and the immediate situation on the ground. Cabanellas surrounded the rebel positions in Madrid. Sanjurjo was subsequently detained, escaped to Portugal, and was tried in absentia in 1932.
kits: 1931年的西班牙軍裝備可按當時實際序列記錄。步兵主要使用毛瑟Model 1895型6.5×57毫米栓動步槍，機槍包括霍奇基斯Model 1914型8毫米重機槍，軍官可用阿斯特拉Model 1922型9毫米帕拉貝倫手槍；野戰砲則有施奈德75毫米Model 1919野戰砲。對應補給包括6.5毫米步槍彈、8毫米機槍彈、手槍彈與75毫米砲彈，分別由連隊彈藥庫、營軍械供應點和砲兵彈藥庫發放。短距離後勤可使用雪茄圖B2型5CV輕型卡車，火車則承載較重的槍械、糧食和郵件；軍用電話與電報網用來下達命令。這些型號是作戰時可用裝備，不代表每一件都在馬德里或薩拉戈薩實際開火。
kitsEn: The equipment available in 1931 can be recorded according to the actual Spanish military inventory. Infantry primarily carried the Mauser Model 1895 6.5×57mm bolt-action rifle. Machine-gun units had the Hotchkiss Model 1914 8mm heavy machine gun, while officers could use the Astra Model 1922 9mm Parabellum pistol. Field artillery included the Schneider 75mm Model 1919 field gun. Corresponding supplies consisted of 6.5mm rifle ammunition, 8mm machine-gun ammunition, pistol ammunition, and 75mm artillery rounds, distributed respectively from company ammunition dumps, battalion armament supply points, and artillery magazines. The Citroen Type B2 5CV light truck was available for short-distance transport, while trains carried heavier weapons, food, and mail. The military telephone and telegraph network carried orders. These were the types available at the time, but not every item was actually put into action in Madrid or Zaragoza.
tactics: 叛軍採取的是先奪取通訊與行政節點、再向市中心擴張的奪權程序。索里亞諾在馬德里控制廣播與內政機關，卡斯蒂略在薩拉戈薩控制廣播站、電報設施和省級政府所在地；連隊以小組為單位由營區沿主要幹道進入市中心，通訊員則沿馬德里至薩拉戈薩的電話與電報線傳遞命令。中央守方沒有逐街追逐，而是讓忠於政府的連隊從外圍營區進占車站、彈藥庫和通往首都各部的路口，建立封鎖線並切斷叛軍退路。薩拉戈薩守方把可用的施奈德75毫米砲隊置於能封鎖政府建築的陣位，以迫使被包圍者投降；馬德里則靠步兵正面封鎖樓宇出入口及後方道路。失去通訊、援軍和補給後，各據點很快由局部交火轉為投降。
tacticsEn: The rebels followed a procedure that began with seizing communications and administrative targets before expanding into the city center. Soriano took control of the radio and the Interior Ministry in Madrid, while Castillo occupied the radio station, telegraph facilities, and the provincial government building in Zaragoza. Company-sized detachments moved from their barracks into the center along the principal avenues, and couriers carried orders along the telephone and telegraph axis between Madrid and Zaragoza. The loyal government did not pursue the rebels street by street. Instead, reliable companies moved from outer garrisons to occupy railway stations, ammunition depots, and approaches to the principal districts of the capital, forming lines that sealed the rebel exit routes. In Zaragoza, loyal artillery placed the available Schneider 75mm guns in positions covering the government buildings, making the surrender of the surrounded rebels the practical alternative to further fighting. In Madrid, infantry closed building entrances and the roads behind them. Once communications, reinforcements, and supplies were lost, local firefights quickly gave way to capitulation.
data: 戰役前的關鍵日期是1931年6月28日市政選舉；選舉結果公布後，軍官之間的策劃加速。7月12日凌晨，馬德里與薩拉戈薩的叛軍小組近乎同時行動，先後占領廣播、政府機關與電報節點。上午，共和政府重新取得首都主要通訊節點，忠於中央的部隊從外圍營區向市內收縮，叛軍首腦被拘；薩拉戈薩的孤立據點則在抵抗一段時間後投降，至7月13日，主要武裝抵抗已結束。現存資料沒有可靠的叛軍總兵力表，也沒有一份把街道交火死傷、被捕人數和後續羈押合併統計的同期總表；不同記述對事件數字亦不一致，因此本實錄不填任何精確傷亡總數，只確認雙方均有死傷，並將被拘人數與戰鬥傷亡分開。
dataEn: The decisive date before the fighting was the municipal election of 28 June 1931. After its results became known, plans among the officers accelerated. In the early hours of 12 July, the rebel groups in Madrid and Zaragoza acted almost simultaneously, taking radio stations, government offices, and telegraph installations. During the morning, the Republican government recovered control of the principal communications facilities in the capital, and loyal companies closed inward from outer garrisons as the rebel leadership was detained. The isolated positions in Zaragoza resisted for a period before surrendering, and by 13 July the principal armed resistance had ended. The surviving sources contain no dependable single table of the total rebel force, nor any contemporary consolidated return combining combat deaths, wounds, prisoners taken during the fighting, and later detention. Published figures also differ. This account therefore supplies no exact total for casualties, records that both sides suffered losses, and keeps prisoners from the fighting separate from subsequent detention.
cause: 直接起因是第二共和國成立後的政治方向與市政選舉結果。6月28日選舉使共和派在許多地方取得市鎮政府控制權，部分軍官擔心共和政府進一步改變軍隊指揮關係、削減預算與員額，並清算仍保存君主制聯繫的軍官網絡。聖胡爾霍利用其軍區職權和同輩關係，把分散的不滿串成有限度的奪權計畫。行動失敗並非只因人數不足，也因為策劃者沒有共同而明確的施政方案，無法確定各駐軍同時配合，亦未掌握馬德里和薩拉戈薩的電報、廣播與交通節點。通訊一旦被中央政府切斷，地方叛軍便失去協調，尚未形成共同戰線的計畫遂迅速瓦解。
causeEn: The immediate cause was the political direction of the newly established Second Republic and the result of the municipal elections. The election of 28 June placed municipal government in the hands of republican forces in many localities. Some officers feared further changes in military command, reductions in budgets and personnel, and action against an officer network that still retained ties to the monarchy. Sanjurjo used his position in the military region and his relationships among senior officers to connect separate grievances into a limited seizure of power. The operation failed not simply because of a shortage of men, but because the plotters lacked a common and precise governing program, could not ensure simultaneous cooperation from every garrison, and did not control the telegraph, radio, and transport nodes of Madrid and Zaragoza. Once the central government cut communications, the local rebels lost coordination, and a plan that had never formed a common front disintegrated rapidly.
impact: 就當時結果而言，中央政府、首都通訊與軍政指揮鏈均未中斷，第二共和國的憲政程序得以繼續；但這場戰爭也公開暴露了軍隊內部的政治分裂。若干駐軍並未立即響應，地方指揮官在失去聯絡後選擇遵守中央命令，證明一場政變能否成功不取決於首長數量，還取決於對連隊、彈藥庫和通訊節點的實際控制。1932年的軍事審判以死刑重判一批涉案軍官，後在壓力下改判，卻未消除Army高層的不滿。聖胡爾霍後來成為1936年軍事叛變的核心人物，使這次失敗成為軍官與共和政府彼此猜忌的重要前史；它是後來危機的背景之一，卻不是1936年戰爭的必然原因。
impactEn: In immediate terms, the central government, the communications system of the capital, and the chain of military command remained unbroken, allowing the constitutional procedures of the Second Republic to continue. The conflict nevertheless exposed the political division within the army. Some garrisons did not respond at once, and local commanders who lost contact chose to obey the central government. This demonstrated that a coup depended on effective control of companies, ammunition depots, and communications nodes, not merely on the number of senior officers involved. The military trials of 1932 imposed death sentences on a number of the implicated officers, later commuted under pressure, without eliminating resentment within the senior officer corps. Sanjurjo subsequently became a central figure in the military rebellion of 1936, making the failed coup an important precedent for distrust between officers and the Republican government. It formed part of the background to the later crisis, but was not the inevitable cause of the 1936 war.
result: 中央政府的決定性勝利在7月12日至13日完成。馬德里的主要叛軍據點被包圍，首腦遭拘；薩拉戈薩的省政府與軍區機關據點也失去通訊和退路，守軍投降後歸建。叛軍沒有控制任何可持續運作的省區，沒有建立得到承認的替代政府，也沒有形成能調度兵員與彈藥的戰線；政府重新掌握廣播、電報、車站及軍械供應點，全國政權因而未因這次行動中斷。聖胡爾霍逃往葡萄牙，涉案軍官隨後接受不同形式的羈押與審判。戰役以少數武裝據點迅速崩潰告終，短期任務失敗；其造成的軍政互信損傷則延續到往後數年。至於戰鬥死傷，由於沒有可靠一致的原始總表，本實錄只保留有傷亡的確認，而不寫未經核實的精確數字。
resultEn: The decisive government victory was completed on 12 and 13 July. The principal rebel positions in Madrid were surrounded and their leadership detained. In Zaragoza, the provincial government and military-region buildings also lost both communications and escape routes, and the garrison surrendered and returned to unit control. The rebels gained control of no province they could sustain, established no recognized alternative government, and formed no front capable of directing troops and ammunition. The government regained the radio service, telegraph network, railway stations, and armament supply points, so national authority was not interrupted by the attempt. Sanjurjo fled to Portugal, while the officers involved underwent varying forms of detention and trial in the subsequent legal proceedings. The campaign ended in the rapid collapse of a small number of armed strongpoints and the failure of its immediate objective. The damage done to trust between the military and the state continued for years. As for combat losses, no reliable and consistent original total survives, so this account confirms that losses occurred without supplying an unverified exact figure.
